[00:04] Welcome to today's tech briefing. Today we cover three major stories: SpaceX targets its most ambitious Starship test yet with a full orbital flight and next-gen Starlink satellites, a rising debate over whether AI chatbots might absorb and steal researchers' proprietary ideas, and a new mathematical study debunking the two-thousand-year-old myth of optical corrections in Athens' Parthenon.

[00:30] Mathematician Challenges 2,000-Year-Old Legend About Parthenon Optical Illusions. For centuries, textbooks and tour guides have taught that the ancient Greeks curved the Parthenon to correct visual illusions. The Roman architect Vitruvius first suggested that a flat building base appears to sag, so ancient masons (石匠；石工。) arched the foundation upward to make it look straight. However, Oxford mathematician Alain Goriely has now debunked (揭穿；推翻（虚假传说）。) this classic story in a new research paper. Goriely examined the temple's architectural refinement (精细调整；微妙改进；精致) (微调；精细调整；精工细作。) and found no scientific proof that these curves were designed as optical corrections. His mathematical calculations revealed that the platform's curvature (曲率；弯曲度。) and subtle architectural adjustments are simply too small to correct how human eyes perceive (感知；察觉；观察到。) straight lines. In fact, the temple columns only swell by 18 millimeters, which is virtually invisible to observers (观察者；参观者。) on the ground. Goriely argues that the myth of optical correction gained popularity without rigorous evidence, leaving the true architectural and aesthetic purpose of the Parthenon's subtle curves an open question. (Source: Hacker News)
数学家挑战两千年来关于帕台农神庙视错觉的历史传说。数百年来，教科书和旅游指南一直宣称古希腊人在建造帕台农神庙时刻意加入了弧度，以修正人眼的视错觉。古罗马建筑学者维特鲁威最早提出，平坦的建筑基座在视觉上容易显得中间下沉，因此古代石匠将地基向上微拱，以使其看起来十分笔直。然而，牛津大学数学家阿兰·戈里利在最新发表的研究论文中推翻了这一经典说法。戈里利仔细研究了神庙的建筑微调结构，发现没有任何科学证据表明这些微曲设计是为了进行光学修正。他的数学计算表明，神庙底座的弧度以及微妙的建筑构造调整幅度过小，根本无法起到矫正人眼感知直线的作用。事实上，神庙立柱中间仅微微向外膨胀了 18 毫米，站在地面的参观者肉眼几乎完全无法察觉。戈里利指出，所谓视错觉修正的说法是在缺乏严谨证据的情况下流传开来的，这使得帕台农神庙微妙弧度背后的真正建筑与美学动机再次成为了一个未解之谜。（来源：Hacker News）

[01:40] Researchers Raise Concerns Over AI Chatbots Absorbing Proprietary (专有的；专利的；受知识产权保护的。) Ideas. As scientists increasingly rely on artificial intelligence to assist their daily workflows, a thorny question has emerged: could chatbots absorb your unreleased (未公开发布的；未公开的。) ideas? A recent dispute reported by The New York Times centers on a prominent mathematics professor who used OpenAI tools to test complex mathematical concepts. When OpenAI shortly afterward announced a breakthrough (重大突破；重大进展。) on a related problem, the professor raised concerns about whether his research queries had influenced their system. While OpenAI firmly denied the claim and stated that user prompts could not have contributed to their discovery, the incident sparked intense anxiety (焦虑；担忧；不安。) across the scientific community. Many researchers, developers, and writers worry that feeding proprietary insights into cloud-based AI systems might compromise their intellectual property. As tech companies compete to build smarter models, the debate highlights the urgent need for clear boundaries (界限；边界；规范。) regarding algorithmic training, data privacy, and scientific attribution (署名权；归属认定；出处说明。). (Source: Hacker News)
学术界担忧 AI 聊天机器人可能吸收并盗用未发表科研创意。随着科学家们日益依赖人工智能来辅助日常科研工作，一个棘手的问题逐渐浮出水面：AI 聊天机器人是否会吸收你尚未公开发表的独创想法？《纽约时报》最近报道了一起引发广泛关注的争议，焦点在于一位知名数学教授曾使用 OpenAI 的工具来推演复杂的数学概念。随后不久，当 OpenAI 宣布在相关数学难题上取得突破时，这位教授对其研究提问是否启发了系统产生了疑虑。尽管 OpenAI 坚决否认了这一质疑，并表示用户的提示词不可能对其科研发现做出贡献，但该事件依然在科学界引发了强烈的焦虑。许多研究人员、开发者和创作者担忧，将专有的前沿见解输入云端 AI 系统可能会损害自身的知识产权。随着科技公司争相构建更强大的模型，这场争论凸显了在算法训练、数据隐私和学术署名权方面确立明确边界的紧迫性。（来源：Hacker News）

[02:47] SpaceX Prepares Starship Flight 14 for First Orbital Mission and Starlink V3 Deployment. SpaceX is preparing for its biggest milestone yet with the upcoming launch of Starship Flight 14, targeted for September 22 from South Texas. While all previous thirteen test flights flew suborbital trajectories (飞行轨迹；弹道路径。), this mission is designed to achieve true orbital insertion (入轨；轨道切入。) around Earth for the first time. The spacecraft will orbit the planet roughly six times over ten hours at an altitude of 275 kilometers before executing a precision (精确；精密。) deorbit burn into the Pacific Ocean. Flight 14 will also attempt to deploy a batch of next-generation Starlink V3 satellites, with each unit offering up to one terabit per second of downlink throughput (吞吐量；传输速率。). SpaceX will not attempt to catch the upper stage with launch tower arms during this flight, choosing instead to focus on orbital safety and satellite separation (（航天器/卫星）分离；脱离。). This ambitious mission marks Starship's crucial leap from experimental (试验性的；实验性质的。) testing to a reliable platform for heavy commercial payloads. (Source: Teslarati)
SpaceX 筹备星舰第 14 次试飞，首次尝试进入地球轨道并部署 V3 星链。SpaceX 正在全力筹备其迄今为止最具里程碑意义的发射任务，星舰第 14 次试飞定于 9 月 22 日在德克萨斯州南部发射场进行。与此前十三次全部采用亚轨道弹道飞行的试飞不同，本次任务的核心目标是首次实现真正的环绕地球入轨飞行。星舰飞船将在 275 公里的高度绕地球飞行约六圈，历时十小时，随后执行精确的离轨点火并溅落于太平洋。第 14 次试飞还将首次尝试在轨部署一批全新一代的星链 V3 卫星，每颗卫星可提供高达每秒 1 Tbps 的下行网络吞吐量。在本次任务中，SpaceX 暂不尝试使用发射塔机械臂在空中捕获二级飞船，而是将主要精力放在入轨安全性与卫星分离测试上。这次雄心勃勃的试飞标志着星舰正从试验验证阶段加速迈向能够运载重型商业载荷的成熟平台。（来源：Teslarati）
